detailedExplanation: Verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Chemistry Curriculum Outline 2026–27 (AQA GCSE Chemistry 8462).

Complete combustion occurs when there is sufficient oxygen and produces carbon dioxide and water. Incomplete combustion occurs when oxygen is limited and can produce carbon monoxide and/or carbon particles as well as water.

Carbon monoxide is toxic because it reduces the blood’s ability to carry oxygen. Sulfur dioxide contributes to acid rain. Nitrogen oxides can contribute to acid rain and respiratory problems. Particulates can damage lungs and reduce air quality.
Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas, so increased emissions from fossil-fuel combustion contribute to climate change. In exam answers, avoid treating all pollutants as if they cause the same effect.

additionalSourceSections.body:
Complete combustion: hydrocarbon + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water
Incomplete combustion: limited oxygen → carbon monoxide and/or carbon (soot) + water
Pollutants: CO₂ · CO · SO₂ · nitrogen oxides · particulates
